executiveSummary: GM0809's identity, Noord-Brabant province and Midden- en West-Brabant safety-region assignment are coherent. The 2025 boundary contains the generated centre and all three BAG places; CBS reports 24,151 residents, while 32 neighbourhood rows sum to 24,130 (-21, -0.087%), consistent with annual rounding/suppression. Four districts, three BAG places and ten BRT settlement labels are present. All ten presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services and pass numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The Loonse en Drunense Duinen, Efteling and three distinct residential cores create large nature-fire, smoke, visitor, evacuation and access mechanisms that registered residents and a generic local seed cannot represent. A controlled ignition at [5.100, 51.640], inside Oost-Loon and a TOP10NL heath polygon, produces municipal fire/smoke 0.436583/0.436581 and 5,216 affected resident-equivalents, yet the source neighbourhood ranks last of 32. Eight individual hazards and compound reuse exactly the same complete T+24 neighbourhood order. Official regional evidence identifies only north-west Loon op Zand as exposed to deep water after a selected Maas-dike breach, while the model selects no breach or footprint and holds 1.231434 normalized inundation stress through T+72, reaching 13,530 affected equivalents and 776,041 person-hours. Municipal evidence distinguishes Kaatsheuvel's high-to-low terrain, limited infiltration, Donge catchment, sewer-overflow interaction and practical cloudburst hotspots, none of which drives pluvial output. Both Brabantse Delta and De Dommel asset records intersect the municipality; current drought measures have their own lifecycle and scope. The logical transport graph has two N261 endpoints on one physical corridor, no station and 21 scheduled stops, but omits Efteling/nature access, independent alternatives and cross-boundary emergency care at ETZ Tilburg. Exact utilities, visitor demand, care, mobility, supply and first-72-hour recovery remain unsupported by live topology, state, resources and actions. Unknown/NoData never means zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0809 Loon op Zand and reports 24,151 residents, density 484/km², 24.4% age 65 or older and 3,300 one-person households.

Thirty-two neighbourhood rows sum to 24,130 residents (-21, -0.087%), 10,575 households and 5,875 rounded residents age 65 or older; deterministic allocation reconciles to the municipality control without changing source rows.

Core population/age/household fields cover 32/32 rows. Home value covers 29, cars per household 28, benefits 29 and doctor/supermarket distance 30; district heating and charging cover 0/32 and remain Unknown/NoData.

CBS OData is annual machine-readable context under CC BY 4.0. It measures registered residents, not Efteling/nature visitors, hotel guests, pupils, patients, commuters, workers, responders, individual vulnerability or preparedness.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipality geography, settlements and road, rail and scheduled-transit inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics; generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS snapshots through 3 September 2026
supports: The generated centre [5.046774448687571, 51.6366390079848] and BAG place labels De Moer, Kaatsheuvel and Loon op Zand lie inside the 2025 municipality boundary.
The bundle contains four districts, 32 neighbourhoods and ten BRT labels: three woonkernen, two deelkernen, two gehuchten and three buurtschappen.

Two logical route records are both N261: one to Waalwijk and one to Tilburg. They are opposite/series municipal endpoints of physical corridor NWB-road-261 and are not two independent routes or additive capacity.

No ProRail station is inside GM0809 and GTFS assigns 21 stop areas, including Efteling, Efteling accommodation and Villa Pardoes stops. Static routes and timetables do not prove incident-time service, accessible vehicles, destinations, evacuation or throughput.
CBS/BRT are CC BY 4.0; BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; NWB-Light and ProRail are CC0. OVapi GTFS is best-effort schedule context without an operational SLA.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Water and sewer programme 2025–2028 and Hemelwatervisie
evidenceSources.edition: Current PWR 2025–2028 page; Hemelwatervisie dated 2016 with 2014 event/model evidence
supports: The current page says the municipality manages wastewater, rainfall, groundwater and surface-water duties under PWR 2025–2028 and retains the Hemelwatervisie as its approach to extreme rain, soil/green storage and reduced paving. Programme intent is not current incident capacity or completed action.

The 2016 vision says Kaatsheuvel falls from about NAP +9.5 m by the dunes to about +1.5 m northwest, has local loam and more limited infiltration westward, while Loon op Zand lies higher on a sand ridge with local low points near Venloonstraat/Ecliptica.

It places surrounding waters in the Donge/Oosterhout–Waalwijk subcatchment and records practical storage/discharge constraints north and west of Kaatsheuvel when combined-sewer overflows operate, causing impaired sewer function and street water. Extreme July 2014 rain exceeded design standards.

An older water-system assessment found no norm-exceeding channel inundation, but the same document records real constraints and calls groundwater knowledge sparse. Old assessment is not an all-clear or current state.

No public live sewer/pump/inlet/blockage state or standard blanket machine licence was identified. Analytical use needs native event/hyetograph, geometry, CRS, resolution, units, uncertainty, licence and NoData.

evidenceSources.publisher: Provincie Noord-Brabant / Regio Hart van Brabant
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Klimaatstresstest regio Hart van Brabant
evidenceSources.edition: Stress-test note dated 7 February 2020; provincial page added 6 July 2020
supports: The regional stress test explicitly includes Loon op Zand and lists several local streets as vulnerable to heavy-rain water nuisance. It is an awareness/planning scenario, not current flooding or a T+72 forecast.

For a Maas-dike breach it says water can flow south and identifies north-west Loon op Zand, where scenario depths can reach five metres. This supports conditional partial-municipality eligibility, not a municipality-wide generic scalar or current threat.

The page separates pluvial, drought, heat, Maas breach and regional-water mechanisms; infrastructure can become impassable during water nuisance. These mechanisms require separate source data and cannot share one population-led neighbourhood order.

The page exposes a PDF/viewer but no stable analytical API, standard reuse licence, fixed update cadence or complete raster NoData contract was identified. Integration requires publisher-confirmed layer, event, CRS, resolution, units, edition, licence and NoData.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Brabantse Delta / Waterschap De Dommel / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current drought lifecycle and public water/drainage assets
evidenceSources.edition: Drought update published 25 August 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026 01:38Z
supports: Brabantse Delta ended the regional daytime irrigation-hours rule from 26 August and stopped using Marksluis for added flow, while saying drought was not over, 2026 was among the five percent driest years and abstraction bans remained in free-draining areas. Exact local polygon/state must be checked; a regional notice is not blanket GM0809 status.

The public water screen assigns 60 points: four sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps, RWZI Kaatsheuvel and 52 weirs. Manager labels are Brabantse Delta for 52, De Dommel for three and generic Waterschap for five, demonstrating cross-authority records rather than one complete system.

Named sewer pumps include Kaatsheuvel, Loon op Zand and De Moer. Registered capacity values lack a normalized comparable unit in the view, while RWZI capacity is null. Register status 'gerealiseerd' is not live operation.

HWH is partial/contributor-dependent official context retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15.250Z under CC BY-SA 4.0 and affectsSimulation=false. It supplies neither connected catchments/topology nor control, power/backup, maintenance, current operation or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Midden- en West-Brabant / Gemeente Loon op Zand / Brandweer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027, local nature-fire preparedness and current phase
evidenceSources.edition: Regional profile created 13 July 2023; dynamic nature-fire phase inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The safety region names Loonse en Drunense Duinen among its largest nature areas and describes forest, heath, peat and dune fire, difficult access, limited firewater, rapid unpredictable spread in drought, smoke, mobility disruption and risk to visitors or less self-reliant locations.

It also names Efteling as a site where many people concentrate in a small area and identifies fire, power loss or technical failure as possible crowd-panic triggers. This is risk/governance context, not incident occupancy, evacuation demand or response capacity.

The municipality says roughly 70% of nature fires arise from human behaviour, warns residents/tourists/recreation visitors and reports annual crisis exercises; an exercise proves preparedness activity, not current ignition, resources or outcome.

The dynamic national page reports Midden- en West-Brabant at phase 1 on access. Phase 1 is ordinary risk with no extraordinary alert, not zero probability, a fuel-moisture observation, forecast or all-clear.
No blanket standard machine-reuse licence was identified on the profile/dynamic pages; publication/edition and issue/retrieval time must be retained.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Loonse en Drunense Duinen and controlled Oost-Loon source-containment test
evidenceSources.edition: Current area page; TOP10NL heath feature 7a907da2-1b5e-595b-ad77-505575ecace9 sourced 1 January 2012 and registered 26 October 2013
supports: Natuurmonumenten identifies the Loonse en Drunense Duinen as a large active sand-dune recreation landscape. The site gives a representative area coordinate; area identity supports visitor/fuel/access eligibility, not an ignition or current occupancy.

Point [5.100, 51.640] lies inside the 2025 CBS Oost-Loon neighbourhood. TOP10NL classifies it as heath from a 2012 aerial source, reported accuracy 0.1; that old CC BY 4.0 land cover is transparent synthetic-source eligibility only.

A focused T+24 wildfire at that point produces municipality severity 0.445052, direct fire 0.436583, smoke 0.436581, 5,216 affected equivalents and 103,714.394 person-hours, yet source-containing Oost-Loon ranks 32nd of 32 at severity 0.365977 while Schrijversbuurt leads at 0.523306.

Neither the old heath classification nor current area page establishes fuel/moisture, perimeter, wind/plume, visitors, route closure, firewater, crews or containment. The run remains a synthetic regression.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Loon op Zand / RIVM / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / Rijksoverheid
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Efteling, acute-care, utility-planning, telecom, education and 72-hour context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: The municipality confirms Efteling in Kaatsheuvel as a theme park, accommodation/event and business destination. Together with the regional crowd-risk profile and named GTFS stops, this establishes material transient demand but not event-time attendance, evacuation or supplies.

RIVM assigns zero full emergency departments inside GM0809 and registers the 24/7 Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis ED in Tilburg outside it, with 38 reported treatment rooms and 35,052 visits in 2025. CC0 v1.1 is dated context, not live route, ambulance, acceptance, occupancy, staff or backup.

One postcode sample 5171WS maps to Enexis TBN Tilburg Noord: withdrawal existing/required/queue 141.1/147.3/62.2 MW with 170 queued requests; injection 131/116.3/37.9 MW with 102 requests; 19 projects and earliest year 2026. Planning is not municipal coverage, feeder topology, live load/outage or project completion; exact licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 34 antenna sites and DUO twelve education records: nine primary, one secondary and two other. RDI WFS has no stated licence/cadence; DUO is daily CC Attribution version unspecified. Neither proves coverage/backhaul/power, occupancy, shelter role, supplies or live operation.

The municipal 'Denk vooruit' page repeats national three-day preparedness guidance including three litres of water per person per day. Guidance is not measured household stock, distribution capacity or completed action.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Enexis, Brabant Water, gas, telecom, wastewater or drainage topology, live state, backup endurance, priority users, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.
Nature-fire outcomes require current ignition/perimeter, fuels/moisture, wind/plume, visitors, access, firewater and suppression; current phase 1 and an old heath polygon are not an event.
Efteling and nature occupancy, accessibility needs, gate/parking/transport/egress and supplies are unavailable as a reviewed time-valid public operational feed; resident population cannot substitute.
Maas breach outcomes require hydrograph, defence/breach and a connected north-west footprint; pluvial requires rain, terrain/soil/groundwater, sewers/overflows, Donge receiving level and controls.
Static NWB and GTFS omit local route, bridge, bus, venue/nature access, ambulance/freight/evacuation throughput and restoration; zero NDW matches never proves open.

Affected population is a resident-equivalent synthetic index and deprived person-hours is weighted event-attributable service deprivation, not casualties, evacuees, visitors, patients or customer interruption-hours.
Dynamic drought, fire, route, care and utility context can change after completion; stale, empty, out-of-scope or superseded data must degrade to Unknown.
